articles.title: Saudi-led strikes kill at least 27 in Yemen's Sanaa, Houthis say
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition air strikes killed 27 people, most of them women and children, in Yemen’s Sanaa province, the Houthis said on Saturday. The Houthi-run health ministry told the group’s Saba news agency that 36 people were also wounded in the strikes on the village of Al-Shariya. Saba reported earlier on Saturday that rescuers were still recovering victims from the rubble, and that warplanes had struck paramedics twice. articles.summary: Yemeni government forces have claimed three air attacks on Houthi positions in the al-Misrakh district of the Taiz governorate. The city of Taiz- which is government-held- has been subject to an ongoing Houthi siege. The blockade has triggered a spiralling humanitarian crisis in the city, as road closures bar vital supplies, including fuel, from entering. articles.title: Saudi strikes in Sanaa kill 11, including women and children, Houthi media says
Houthi media says 11 killed in Saudi strikes on Yemen's Sanaa province
articles.summary: Houthi media said on Saturday that Saudi strikes killed 11 people, including women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, following the return of the country's dormant civil war. "Martyrdom of 11 citizens, among them women and children, in Saudi enemy airstrikes" on homes in the Al-Shariyah area of Sanaa province, the Iran-backed Houthis' Saba news agency said, adding that operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes"…

articles.title: Yemen: 30 dead in strikes on Taiz market
articles.summary: At least 30 people have reportedly been killed in an attack on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, with Houthi rebels blaming Saudi airstrikes. Government forces and local authorities have disputed the claim, instead accusing the Houthis of indiscriminate fire. The province has witnessed intense clashes in recent weeks and is home to around half of the more than 300,000 people displaced by the latest fighting. Caroline Baum reports.
